items.title: Complex Polynomials as a Product of Linear Factors (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko "1.2 Complex Polynomials as a Product of Linear Factors" chhapti hai. Number par neeche wala box dekhiye.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Number 1.2 kitab mein doosri dafa chhapa hai; 1.2 pehle hi "Equality of Two Complex Numbers" ke liye aa chuka hai. Kitab ki tarteeb ke hisaab se yeh section 1.3 hona chahiye (is ka agla sub-heading 1.3.1 chhapa hai). Is liye hum yahan printed title number ke baghair rakhte hain. Aap ke parhne par is ka koi asar nahin, sirf numbering ki ghalti hai.

Is sabaq mein hum seekhenge ke complex polynomial kya hota hai, aur use chhote chhote linear factors (degree 1 wale tukron) mein kaise toda jata hai. Pichli classes mein aap ne \(x^{2} - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)\) jaisi factorization ki thi. Lekin aap ne yeh bhi dekha hoga ke \(x^{2} + 4\) jaisa expression real numbers mein toot hi nahin sakta. Aaj hum dekhenge ke complex numbers ki madad se har polynomial toot jata hai. Yeh is unit ka bohat aham khayal hai.

Pehle definition. Complex polynomial \(P(z)\) aisa polynomial function hai jis ka variable complex \(z\) ho aur coefficients (terms ke saath lage numbers) bhi complex numbers hon. Is ki general shakal yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: P of z equals a n z to the power n plus a n minus 1 z to the power n minus 1 plus and so on plus a 1 z plus a 0

blocks.text: Yahan \(a_{n}, a_{n-1}, \dots, a_{1}, a_{0}\) complex numbers hain (aur \(a_{n} \ne 0\)), aur \(n \ge 0\) ek integer (poora number) hai jo polynomial ki degree (sab se bari power) batata hai.

Kuch misaalein dekhiye: \(P_{1}(z) = (1 - i)z + 3i\) linear (degree 1) hai, \(P_{2}(z) = (5 - 4i)z^{2} + (2 + i)z + (3 - 4i)\) quadratic (degree 2) hai, aur \(P_{3}(z) = (2 - i)z^{3} + 2z^{2}i + (5 + 3i)\) cubic (degree 3) hai. Agar \(n = 0\) ho to \(P(z)\) sirf ek constant reh jata hai, isay constant polynomial kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Degree pehchaanne ka tareeqa: \(z\) ki sab se bari power dekhiye. \(P_{1}\) mein 1, \(P_{2}\) mein 2, \(P_{3}\) mein 3.
Us sab se bari power ke saath laga number \(a_{n}\) leading coefficient (sab se aage wala coefficient) kehlata hai. Yeh zero nahin ho sakta, warna woh term gayab ho jayegi aur degree kam ho jayegi.
Ek dilchasp baat: \(z^{2} + 4\) jaisa real polynomial bhi complex polynomial hai, kyun ke har real number ek complex number hai jis ka imaginary part 0 hai. Yani complex polynomials ki duniya mein purane saare polynomials bhi shamil hain.
Complex polynomials ki ek bunyadi khoobi yeh hai ke inhein hamesha linear factors ke product mein toda ja sakta hai. Yeh baat kis buniyad par kehte hain? Ek mashhoor theorem par:
Fundamental theorem of algebra ke mutabiq, degree \(n \ge 1\) wale polynomial ke complex number system \(C\) mein bilkul \(n\) roots hote hain.

Is theorem ka ek corollary (theorem se seedha nikalne wala natija) kehta hai ke degree \(n\) wale kisi bhi polynomial \(P(z)\) ko \(C\) mein poori tarah ek constant \(a\) aur \(n\) linear factors mein toda ja sakta hai, is shakal mein:

blocks.text_alt: P of z equals a times (z minus z 1) times (z minus z 2) and so on up to (z minus z n), equation 1

blocks.text: Jahan \(z_{1}, z_{2}, \dots, z_{n}\) polynomial ke complex roots hain. Iska matlab yeh hai: agar humein polynomial equation ke roots maloom hon, to equation (1) laga kar \(P(z)\) ko \(n\) linear factors mein tod sakte hain. Khaas taur par, agar \(z_{1}\) aur \(z_{2}\) polynomial equation \(P(z) = 0\) ke roots hon, to \(P(z) = (z - z_{1})(z - z_{2})\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is ko aise samjhein: roots aur factors ek hi sikke ke do rukh hain. Root \(z_{1}\) mil gaya to factor \((z - z_{1})\) mil gaya, aur factor mil gaya to root mil gaya.
Formula (1) mein constant \(a\) asal mein leading coefficient \(a_{n}\) hi hai. Is liye aakhri statement \(P(z) = (z - z_{1})(z - z_{2})\) sirf us quadratic ke liye hai jis ka leading coefficient 1 ho. Agar leading coefficient 1 nahin, to use aage rakhna zaroori hai: misaal ke taur par \(2z^{2} - 12z + 50 = 2(z - z_{1})(z - z_{2})\) (Example 10 mein aap yeh dekhenge).
"Bilkul \(n\) roots" ka matlab hai ke dohraya hua (repeated) root utni dafa gina jata hai jitni dafa woh aata hai: \(z^{2} = 0\) mein root 0 do dafa gina jata hai.

Ab woh misaal dekhte hain jo saari baat saaf kar deti hai. Polynomial \(P(x) = x^{2} + 4\), jis ke coefficients real hain, ka koi real root nahin (kyun ke \(x^{2}\) kabhi \(-4\) nahin ho sakta). Is liye real coefficients wale linear polynomials mein yeh nahin toot sakta. Lekin agar hum ise complex polynomial \(P(z) = z^{2} + 4\) maanein, to yeh aasani se do linear factors mein toot jata hai:

blocks.text_alt: z squared plus 4 equals (z plus 2 i) times (z minus 2 i)

blocks.text: Jahan \(2i\) aur \(-2i\) equation \(z^{2} + 4 = 0\) ke complex roots hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh kaam kyun karta hai? \((2i)^{2} = 4i^{2} = -4\), is liye \(z^{2} + 4\) ko \(z^{2} - (2i)^{2}\) likh sakte hain. Yeh do squares ka farq (difference of two squares) hai: \(a^{2} - b^{2} = (a + b)(a - b)\). Bas \(+4\) ko \(-(2i)^{2}\) dekhne wali nazar chahiye!
Real numbers mein \(z^{2} + 4\) nahin toot-ta, lekin \(C\) mein hamesha toot jata hai. Khud sochiye: \(z^{2} + 9\) ke factors kya honge? (Jawab: \((z + 3i)(z - 3i)\).)

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Agar \(P(z)\) ek polynomial function ho, to \(z\) ki woh values jo \(P(z) = 0\) ko poora karti hain, function \(P(z)\) ke zeros kehlati hain, aur polynomial equation \(P(z) = 0\) ke roots.

Ab factorization ke teen tareeqe kitab ki misaalon se seekhte hain: grouping (jori bana kar common nikalna), middle term ko torna (split karna), aur Rational Root Theorem ke saath synthetic division. Har misaal mein pehle dekhiye ke kaun sa tareeqa kyun chuna gaya.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: Factorize the polynomial \(P(z) = z^{2} + (1 - i)z - i\).
steps:
Given: \(P(z) = z^{2} + (1 - i)z - i\).
To find: is ke linear factors.
Method: sab se pehle polynomial ko ghor se dekhiye. Beech wali term mein ek bracket \((1 - i)\) hai. Agar ise khol dein to chaar terms ban jayengi, aur chaar terms ko do do ki jori mein grouping (common factor nikal kar) se factorize karna sab se aasan raasta hai.

Step 1: Bracket kholein
\[P(z) = z^{2} + z - iz - i\]
Kyun: \((1 - i)z = 1 \cdot z - i \cdot z = z - iz\). Ab chaar terms hain jinhein do do ki jori mein baanta ja sakta hai: \((z^{2} + z)\) aur \((-iz - i)\).

Step 2: Har jori se common factor nikaalein
\[= z(z + 1) - i(z + 1)\]
Kyun: \(z^{2} + z\) mein \(z\) common hai, aur \(-iz - i\) mein \(-i\) common hai. Dekhiye kamaal: dono joriyon mein se ek hi bracket \(z + 1\) bachti hai. Grouping mein yahi nishani hai ke aap sahi raaste par hain.
Dhyan dein: \(-i\) common nikaalte waqt \(-i \cdot 1 = -i\) hona chahiye, is liye bracket mein \(+1\) aata hai, \(-1\) nahin.

Step 3: \((z + 1)\) ko common nikaalein
\[= (z + 1)(z - i)\]
Kyun: same bracket dono terms mein hai, is liye woh poore expression ka common factor hai. Jo bacha (\(z\) aur \(-i\)) woh doosri bracket ban gaya.

Tasdeeq:
Factors ko wapas multiply kar ke dekhte hain:
\[(z + 1)(z - i) = z^{2} - iz + z - i\]
\[= z^{2} + (1 - i)z - i\]
Yeh \(P(z)\) ke barabar hai. Is ke zeros \(z = -1\) aur \(z = i\) hain (har factor ko zero rakhne se).

blocks.title: Example 7
steps:
Given: \(P(z) = z^{2} - 4iz + 12\).
To find: is ke linear factors.
Method: yeh quadratic hai, aur yahan middle term ko split karna (torna) hai, bilkul jaise aap \(x^{2} - 5x + 6\) mein karte the. Humein do aise numbers chahiye jin ka jor (sum) \(-4i\) ho aur zarb (product) \(12\) ho. Pehli nazar mein mushkil lagta hai kyun ke middle mein \(i\) hai aur constant mein nahin. Chaal yeh hai ke \(12\) ko \(-12i^{2}\) likh dein; is se pata chalta hai ke \(-6i\) aur \(2i\) kaam karte hain.

Step 1: \(12\) ko \(i^{2}\) ki madad se likhein
\[P(z) = z^{2} - 4iz - (-12)\]
\[= z^{2} - 4iz - i^{2}12\]
Kyun: \(i^{2} = -1\), is liye \(-i^{2}12 = -(-1)12 = 12\). Value bilkul nahin badli, sirf shakal badli hai. Is shakal mein constant term mein bhi \(i^{2}\) aa gaya, ab woh do numbers dhoondna aasan hai jin mein \(i\) ho.

Step 2: Middle term ko split karein
\[= z^{2} - i6z + i2z - i^{2}12\]
Kyun: \(-6i + 2i = -4i\) (middle coefficient wapas) aur \((-6i)(2i) = -12i^{2} = 12\) (constant term wapas). Dono shartein poori hain, is liye yeh sahi jori hai.

Step 3: Jori bana kar common nikaalein
\[= z(z - 6i) + 2i(z - 6i)\]
Kyun: \(z^{2} - 6iz\) mein \(z\) common hai. \(2iz - 12i^{2}\) mein \(2i\) common hai, kyun ke \(2i \cdot 6i = 12i^{2}\); is liye bracket mein \(z - 6i\) bachta hai. Phir se dono brackets same aa gayin.

Step 4: \((z - 6i)\) common nikaalein
\[= (z - 6i)(z + 2i)\]
Kyun: same bracket dono terms mein hai, us ko bahar nikaala aur baaqi \(z + 2i\) doosri bracket ban gayi.

Tasdeeq:
\[(z - 6i)(z + 2i) = z^{2} + 2iz - 6iz - 12i^{2}\]
\[= z^{2} - 4iz + 12\]
Yeh \(P(z)\) ke barabar hai. Dhyan dein ke \(-12i^{2}\) ko \(+12\) banana na bhoolein, yahi jagah sab se zyada ghalti hoti hai. Is ke zeros \(z = 6i\) aur \(z = -2i\) hain.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: Factorize the polynomial \(P(z) = z^{3} + (1 + i)z^{2} + iz\).
steps:
Given: \(P(z) = z^{3} + (1 + i)z^{2} + iz\).
To find: is ke linear factors.
Method: cubic (degree 3) dekh kar ghabrayein nahin. Pehle dekhiye: kya har term mein koi cheez common hai? Haan, har term mein \(z\) hai. To pehle \(z\) common nikaalenge; peechhe ek quadratic bachega, jise Example 6 ki tarah grouping se torenge.

Step 1: \(z\) common nikaalein
\[P(z) = z[z^{2} + (1 + i)z + i]\]
Kyun: \(z\) har term ko divide karta hai (\(z^{3} = z \cdot z^{2}\), \((1+i)z^{2} = z \cdot (1+i)z\), \(iz = z \cdot i\)). Is se ek linear factor \(z\) to foran mil gaya.

Step 2: Bracket kholein
\[= z[z^{2} + z + iz + i]\]
Kyun: \((1 + i)z = z + iz\). Ab bracket ke andar chaar terms hain jinhein jori mein baant sakte hain.

Step 3: Jori bana kar common nikaalein
\[= z[z(z + 1) + i(z + 1)]\]
Kyun: \(z^{2} + z\) mein \(z\) common hai aur \(iz + i\) mein \(i\) common hai. Dono mein se \(z + 1\) bachta hai.

Step 4: \((z + 1)\) common nikaalein
\[= z[(z + 1)(z + i)]\]
\[= z(z + 1)(z + i)\]
Yahi linear factors hain.
Kyun: same bracket dono terms mein hai. Ab teen factors hain, aur har ek ki degree 1 hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[(z + 1)(z + i) = z^{2} + (1 + i)z + i\]
Ise \(z\) se multiply karein to \(z^{3} + (1 + i)z^{2} + iz = P(z)\) mil jata hai. Ghor karein: cubic ke teen linear factors aaye, bilkul jaise theorem kehta hai. Is ke zeros \(0, -1, -i\) hain.

blocks.text: Ab tak har polynomial mein grouping ka raasta saaf nazar aa raha tha. Lekin agar koi cubic aisa ho jis mein na koi cheez common ho aur na grouping bane, tab kya karein? Tab humein pehle ek root khud dhoondna parta hai. Is ke liye kitab ek aala (tool) deti hai:

blocks.title: Key Concept
blocks.text:
Rational Root Theorem ek mathematical tool hai jis se integer coefficients wali polynomial equation ke tamam mumkina rational roots (fraction ki shakal wale roots) dhoonde jate hain. Rational root theorem ke mutabiq:
Agar polynomial \(P(x) = a_{n}x^{n} + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + \dots + a_{1}x + a_{0}\) ke coefficients integers hon, to har rational root \(\frac{p}{q}\) (sab se chhoti shakal mein) yeh shartein poori karta hai:
(i) \(p\) constant term \(a_{0}\) ka factor hai.
(ii) \(q\) leading coefficient \(a_{n}\) ka factor hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Istemal ka tareeqa, qadam ba qadam:
1. Constant term \(a_{0}\) ke saare factors likhein (\(\pm\) ke saath).
2. Leading coefficient \(a_{n}\) ke saare factors likhein.
3. Har mumkina fraction \(p/q\) banayein; yeh "umeedwar" (candidates) hain.
4. Ek ek kar ke polynomial mein rakhein, jab tak \(P = 0\) na aa jaye.
Yaad rakhiye, theorem sirf umeedwar deta hai; yeh wada nahin karta ke un mein se koi zaroor root hoga. Jaise hi ek root \(r\) mil jaye, \(z - r\) ek factor hai, aur synthetic division se degree ek kam ho jati hai: cubic se quadratic, jise hum aaram se hal kar sakte hain.

blocks.title: Example 9
steps:
Given: \(P(z) = z^{3} - 3z^{2} + z + 5\), ek cubic jis ke coefficients integers hain.
To find: is ke linear factors.
Method: yahan har term mein koi common cheez nahin aur grouping bhi nahin banti. Is liye teen marhalon ka plan hai: (1) Rational Root Theorem se ek root dhoondein, (2) us factor se synthetic division kar ke cubic ko quadratic mein badlein, (3) bache hue quadratic ko quadratic formula se hal karein.

Step 1: Mumkina rational roots ki list
Constant term \(a_{0} = 5\): factors \(p = \pm1, \pm5\). Leading coefficient \(a_{3} = 1\): factors \(q = \pm1\).
\[\frac{p}{q} = \pm1,\ \pm5\]
Rational Root Theorem ke mutabiq equation ke mumkina roots ±1 aur ±5 hain.
Kyun: har rational root \(p/q\) mein \(p\) ko 5 ka factor aur \(q\) ko 1 ka factor hona chahiye. 5 prime hai, is liye list bohat chhoti hai: sirf chaar umeedwar.

Step 2: Umeedwaron ko check karein
\[P(1) = 1 - 3 + 1 + 5 = 4 \ne 0\]
\[P(-1) = (-1)^{3} - 3(-1)^{2} + (-1) + 5\]
\[= -1 - 3 - 1 + 5 = 0\]
To \(z = -1\) root hai aur \(z + 1\) \(P(z)\) ka factor hai.
Kyun: factor theorem kehta hai ke agar \(P(a) = 0\) ho to \(z - a\) factor hai. Yahan \(a = -1\), is liye factor \(z - (-1) = z + 1\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \((-1)^{2} = +1\), is liye \(-3(-1)^{2} = -3\); aur \((-1)^{3} = -1\). Negative numbers ki powers mein sign ki ghalti aam hai.

Step 3: \(-1\) se synthetic division
\[\begin{array}{r|rrrr} -1 & 1 & -3 & 1 & 5 \\ & & -1 & 4 & -5 \\ \hline & 1 & -4 & 5 & 0 \end{array}\]
Pehla 1 neeche utaar lein; \(1 \times (-1) = -1\), \(-3 + (-1) = -4\); \(-4 \times (-1) = 4\), \(1 + 4 = 5\); \(5 \times (-1) = -5\), \(5 + (-5) = 0\).
\[z^{3} - 3z^{2} + z + 5 = (z + 1)(z^{2} - 4z + 5) \ \text{...(i)}\]
Kyun: synthetic division lambi division ka chhota tareeqa hai. Aakhri row ke numbers \(1, -4, 5\) quotient \(z^{2} - 4z + 5\) ke coefficients hain, aur aakhir ka 0 remainder hai. Remainder 0 aana is baat ki tasdeeq hai ke \(z + 1\) waqai factor hai. Yaad rakhiye: division mein root \(-1\) likha jata hai, factor \(z + 1\) nahin.

Step 4: \(z^{2} - 4z + 5 = 0\) ko quadratic formula se hal karein
Yahan \(a = 1,\ b = -4,\ c = 5\).
\[z = \dfrac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2} - 4(1)(5)}}{2(1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - 20}}{2} = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{-4}}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{4 \pm 2i}{2}\]
\[z = 2 \pm i\]
Kyun: yeh quadratic aasani se split nahin hota, is liye quadratic formula sab se mehfooz raasta hai. \(\sqrt{-4} = \sqrt{4}\sqrt{-1} = 2i\). Phir 2 se divide karte waqt numerator ki dono terms divide hongi: \(4/2 = 2\) aur \(2i/2 = i\). Kitab yahan ghalti se \(2 \pm 2i\) chhapti hai (is misaal ke baad "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye).

Step 5: Quadratic ke factors likhein
\[z^{2} - 4z + 5 = (z - (2 + i))(z - (2 - i))\]
\[= (z - 2 - i)(z - 2 + i)\]
Kyun: corollary ke mutabiq leading coefficient 1 wala quadratic jis ke roots \(z_{1}, z_{2}\) hon, \((z - z_{1})(z - z_{2})\) ke barabar hai. Bracket kholte waqt minus dono terms par lagta hai: \(-(2 - i) = -2 + i\).

Step 6: Equation (i) mein rakhein
\[z^{3} - 3z^{2} + z + 5\]
\[= (z + 1)(z - 2 - i)(z - 2 + i)\]
Kyun: (i) mein quadratic ki jagah us ke do linear factors rakh diye, to cubic ke teen linear factors mil gaye, jaisa Fundamental theorem of algebra kehta hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[(z - 2 - i)(z - 2 + i) = (z - 2)^{2} - i^{2}\]
\[= z^{2} - 4z + 4 + 1 = z^{2} - 4z + 5\]
\[(z + 1)(z^{2} - 4z + 5) = z^{3} - 3z^{2} + z + 5\]
Dono products asal polynomial wapas dete hain. Pehli line mein \((A - B)(A + B) = A^{2} - B^{2}\) use kiya, jahan \(A = z - 2\) aur \(B = i\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
1. Sawal mein "Factorize the + polynomial" chhapa hai; yeh faltu "+" nahin hona chahiye. Sahi sawal: "Factorize the polynomial \(P(z) = z^{3} - 3z^{2} + z + 5\)".
2. Quadratic formula wale step mein kitab \(z = 2 \pm 2i\) likhti hai, jab ke \(\frac{4 \pm 2i}{2} = 2 \pm i\). (Agar roots \(2 \pm 2i\) hote to quadratic \(z^{2} - 4z + 8\) banta, \(z^{2} - 4z + 5\) nahin.) Kitab ki agli lines sahi roots \(2 + i\) aur \(2 - i\) hi use karti hain, is liye aakhri jawab \((z + 1)(z - 2 - i)(z - 2 + i)\) durust hai.

blocks.caption: Example 9 ki synthetic division kaise chalti hai (divisor ka root −1)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Degree \(n \ge 1\) wale complex polynomial ke \(C\) mein bilkul \(n\) roots hote hain (Fundamental theorem of algebra).
2. Corollary: \(P(z) = a(z - z_{1})(z - z_{2})\dots(z - z_{n})\), jahan \(a\) leading coefficient hai.
3. \(P(z)\) ke zeros = equation \(P(z) = 0\) ke roots. Root \(r\) mila to factor \(z - r\) mila.
4. Tareeqa chunne ka sawal: kya koi cheez common hai? (Example 8) Kya chaar terms ki grouping banti hai? (Examples 6, 8) Kya middle term split ho sakti hai? (Example 7) Kuch na bane to Rational Root Theorem + synthetic division + quadratic formula (Example 9).
5. Aakhir mein factors ko multiply kar ke hamesha check karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Factors likhte waqt leading coefficient \(a\) chhor dena. Bachne ka tareeqa: pehle dekhiye \(z^{n}\) ke saath kya laga hai.
2. Check karte waqt \(i^{2} = -1\) bhool jana: \((z - 6i)(z + 2i)\) mein \(-12i^{2} = +12\) hai.
3. \(\frac{4 \pm 2i}{2}\) mein sirf 4 ko 2 se divide karna: dono terms divide hongi, jawab \(2 \pm i\) (kitab khud yahan phisli hai).
4. Root se factor banate waqt sign ulat dena: root \(z = a\) ka factor \(z - a\) hai, is liye root \(-1\) ka factor \(z + 1\) hai, \(z - 1\) nahin.
5. Rational Root Theorem ke umeedwaron mein minus wale (\(-1, -5\)) bhool jana; is misaal mein asal root \(-1\) hi tha.
